findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the soda nozzles in the kitchen and lobby were soiled with debris. The PIC removed the soda nozzles and washed, rinsed, and sanitized them during the inspection. The inspector suggests increasing the frequency of cleaning. Ensure that the soda nozzles are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there are several small holes in the wall in the dry storage area (the room with the prep table, microwave, and soda lines). The holes must be filled (ex. caulking) to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. Ensure the holes are filled by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the knife holder on the prep line has an accumulation of food debris on the bottom. The knife holder must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid contaminating food contact surfaces. Ensure that the knife holder is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the tea dispenser filter holder in the lobby has an accumulation of soil residues. The dispenser must be cleaned on a regular basis to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the tea dispenser is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed employees have not completed the food handler training. All employees who handle food and do not have the CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all required employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Observed there is not a written procedure to respond to vomit and diarrheal events at the facility. The PIC was given a written procedure during the inspection. Ensure that the written procedure is kept at the facility.

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink is not functioning. The PIC stated they are using the triple sink to wash their hands. Paper towels and soap are available at the triple sink and sufficient handwashing was observed during the inspection. The PIC said they are in the process of getting the hand sink fixed. A plumber should be coming in the next 1-3 days. Ensure that once repaired hand washing only occurs in designated hand washing sinks
. 
5-203.11: (A) Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEESS. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed a drip coming from the top portion of the walk-in cooler. The PIC was aware of the issue and is using buckets to catch the water. The drip was worsened today due to heavy rainfall last night. The PIC said they are working on fixing the issue. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the following repeat violations from the previous inspections dated 02/22/2023 and 08/30/2022 have not been fixed:  

- The tile to the left of the mop sink which was cracked and in-need of repair/replacement is still is disrepair. Areas subject to food/moisture must be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that these tile are repaired/replaced and sealed appropriately prior to the next routine inspection.
- Caulking around the mop sink is dirty, not-smooth and cracking. The mop sink is subject to large amounts of moisture and thus is required to be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that the caulking around the mop sink is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
- The corner trim and wall board along the right edge of the door to the walk-in cooler is still not properly attached and there is a gap between the trim and the wall board. Ensure that this portion of the wall is repaired to create a surface which is smooth and easily cleanable. 
- The caulking behind the triple sink is missing/deteriorating/molding and is in need of replacement. Ensure that the rear of the triple sink is sealed to create a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface.

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mops being stored with the heads in the mop sink. The PIC moved the mops during the inspection. Ensure that mops are placed in a position that allows the head to air dry.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the employee currently working does not have their food handlers training completed. The PIC stated that no other employees have their food handlers training. Ensure that within 30 days of hire all employees complete food handler training and copies of the certificates are kept at the facility.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
